newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-MANSELL RULES OUT RETURN TO FORMULA ONE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-MANSELL RULES OUT RETURN TO FORMULA ONE.

text.p: Former world motor racing champion Nigel Mansell of Britain ruled out a return to Formula One in 1997 on Tuesday, less than a week after successfully testing a Jordan Grand Prix car in Barcelona.
Mansell, who won the 1992 world title for Williams, explained that his schedule outside the sport would leave him insufficient time for the Jordan team.

"I thoroughly enjoyed my test in Barcelona and the professionalism and atmosphere of the Jordan team was as good as any I have ever worked with," said Mansell, 43. "Eddie Jordan has created something very special. Having seen their facility, and the 1997 car, I honestly believe that the team can enjoy success next season and become serious contenders."

He continued: "The idea of the test was originally to have some fun, but my natural competitive instinct took over very quickly and a return to Formula One with Jordan became a serious possibility. However, after consultations with my family and business advisers, I quickly came to realise my schedule would not permit me to give sufficient time to the Jordan team and their sponsors."

Team owner Eddie Jordan added: "It was an honour to have Nigel in our car and we were very, very impressed with his approach and attitude. I believe Nigel can still be a winner, but I appreciate the honesty of his decision."
Jordan said the team will continue to explore ways for Mansell to have an involvement with the team.
It now seems likely that another Briton, Martin Brundle, will line up alongside German Ralf Schumacher for Jordan next season.
